statement: Let n = len(events). For 0 <= i < n write start_i = events[i][0], end_i = events[i][1], value_i = events[i][2]. Call a set T of indices feasible when |T| <= 2 and, for every two distinct i,j in T, either end_i < start_j or end_j < start_i. Define S = { sum_{i in T} value_i | T is feasible }, with the empty sum equal to 0. Then the function returns a result r and r = max(S).
preconditions: events has length n with 2 <= n <= 100000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, events[i] has length 3; writing start_i = events[i][0], end_i = events[i][1], value_i = events[i][2], we have 1 <= start_i <= end_i <= 1000000000 and 1 <= value_i <= 1000000.
